skill.name: mantis-dedupe
skill.description: Consolidates raw security findings to eliminate redundant reports. Use when raw findings have been generated by the researcher and need consolidation before review. Don't use for initial code auditing or patch generation.
skill.summary: Consolidate duplicate security findings while preserving provenance, regression candidates, and transaction history.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: The 160 static alerts describe Markdown notation, legitimate workspace operations, and defensive snapshot checks rather than the alleged execution or reconnaissance threats. Semantic review found unsafe helper reuse and potential disclosure of sensitive vulnerability summaries through external embeddings. No evidence found of malicious intent or instructions to manipulate this audit.

remediation.issue: Existing helper scripts are trusted based only on a reproducible version comment.
remediation.suggestion: Regenerate helpers from trusted instructions or verify their complete contents against a trusted digest before execution; reject unexpected symlinks and untrusted ownership.

remediation.issue: Embedding fallback can send sensitive vulnerability summaries to an external provider without an explicit disclosure gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval before external embeddings, document transmitted fields, redact sensitive details, and provide a local embedding option.

content.value_statement: Repeated security findings increase review effort and can obscure regressions. This skill guides consolidation while preserving provenance, active regression candidates, and transaction history.
actual_capabilities: Compare current findings with archived findings using location, title, and pairwise discovery provenance.
Keep unmatched snapshot findings active and annotate potential regressions against resolved archived issues.
Merge current-batch duplicates at the same line-inclusive location while preserving primary identifiers, metadata, and history.
Stage duplicate records without permanent deletion and append transaction records for each move.
Guide exact lineage matching, standardized root-cause summaries, and configured embedding similarity comparisons with CWE guards.
Group large finding queues by file or component before checking duplicates.
limitations: This package contains instructions only; it does not include the merge helper, embedding engine, or lineage database.
It requires existing finding files and suitable workspace state; it does not perform initial security auditing or generate patches.
Semantic fallback depends on configured embedding infrastructure and may disclose sensitive summaries to an external provider.
Existing helper reuse checks a version comment, not content integrity; helpers require independent verification before execution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Security Review Queue
use_cases.description: Consolidate repeated reports at identical locations while retaining severity, supporting details, and review history.

use_cases.title: Preserve Regression Candidates Across Passes
use_cases.description: Compare new findings with archived records and retain possible regressions when discovery snapshots differ.

use_cases.title: Maintain Traceable Finding Pipelines
use_cases.description: Process large queues with grouped comparisons, provenance checks, staged duplicates, and transaction records.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Small Finding Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing findings and identify duplicate candidates. Explain the matching evidence before changing any files.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Current-Batch Duplicates
prompt_templates.prompt: Consolidate findings with identical line-inclusive locations and matching titles. Preserve provenance and history, stage duplicates, and summarize changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: merge repeated reports within one batch.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Findings Across Snapshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current and archived findings using pairwise discovery provenance. Keep unmatched findings active and annotate regressions against resolved archived issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preserve distinct findings across review passes.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Large Queue Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Group findings by component, verify helpers before execution, and apply snapshot-gated matching. Require approval before external embeddings and summarize staged moves.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate large queues and external integration boundaries.

output_examples.input: Two findings describe the same flaw at the same line and share discovery provenance.
output: One primary finding retains its identifier and the highest reported severity.
Descriptions, code paths, and history are consolidated.
The duplicate is staged with linkage to the primary finding, and its move is logged.

output_examples.input: A new finding matches a resolved archived issue, but their discovery snapshots differ.
output: A possible duplicate hint references the archived finding.
History records a possible regression; the finding is not moved to staging.

output_examples.input: Two findings have matching signatures and titles but identify different lines in the same file.
output: The findings remain separate because their line-inclusive locations differ.
Signature agreement alone does not justify a duplicate status or staged removal.

best_practices: Back up workspace state and review matching evidence before applying consolidation.
Verify helper contents independently before execution; a version comment does not establish trust.
Approve external embedding use explicitly and redact sensitive vulnerability details before transmission.
anti_patterns: Marking findings as duplicates based only on signatures, without line-inclusive location agreement.
Suppressing potential regressions or merging findings from different discovery versions.
Executing existing helpers solely because their version comments match.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Workspace file access and command execution are needed to apply merges.

faq.question: Does this skill discover new vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It consolidates existing findings and identifies possible regressions during archive comparisons. Initial auditing and patch generation are outside its scope.

faq.question: Are duplicate files permanently deleted?
faq.answer: No. Duplicates receive status and linkage metadata, move into a staging directory, and generate transaction records.

faq.question: What happens when discovery snapshots differ?
faq.answer: Snapshot-gated archive matches remain active with a possible duplicate hint. Resolved archived matches receive possible regression notes.

faq.question: Does deduplication require an external service?
faq.answer: Exact matching does not inherently require external embeddings. Semantic fallback requires configured embedding infrastructure and defaults to a Vertex AI model.

faq.question: Is an existing helper safe when its version matches?
faq.answer: No. A matching comment does not verify script contents. Independently inspect or regenerate helpers before execution.
